mainTopic: How a חטאת passes its status through absorption, why the עשה of eating does not override the prohibition, and how the list of offerings in ויקרא 7:37 spreads laws to all קדשים
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא on the פסוק 'כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש'. Food takes on a חטאת's status only if it absorbs from the חטאת's meat. Only the spot that absorbed is affected, and it is cut off. Touching the sinews, bones, horns or hooves does nothing. The food becomes like the חטאת: it is פסול if the חטאת was פסולה, and it is eaten under the חטאת's stricter rules if the חטאת was כשרה. The גמרא asks why the עשה of eating the sacrificial meat doesn't override the prohibition. רבא answers that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה connected to the מקדש, and he proves this from the bones of the קרבן פסח. רב אשי answers instead that 'יקדש' is itself an עשה, so one עשה cannot override a לא תעשה joined by another עשה. Next, שמואל in the name of רבי אליעזר applies the absorption rule to all קדשים, using the פסוק that lists all the offerings together. The גמרא explains two lessons from that list: every offering needs a knife, like an עולה (learned from אברהם at the עקידה), and every offering is eaten only by male כהנים, like a מנחה. When the גמרא asks which offering actually needs that second lesson, it answers 'תנאי היא', and the next amud explains this disagreement.

steps.title: Only absorption counts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its first point: the touching food only takes on the חטאת's status if it absorbs from the חטאת's meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule applies only once the other food absorbs something from the חטאת's meat.
steps.whatsHappening: We are picking up at the last words of a ברייתא that started earlier. It says that simply touching is not enough; the חטאת's status passes only when there is real absorption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'whatever touches its flesh,' but the ברייתא reads this as needing actual absorption, not just surface contact. This sets the basic condition for everything that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, the קרבן this whole teaching is about

phrases.english: unless it is absorbed into its meat.
phrases.notes: 'Its meat' is the meat of the חטאת. These words finish a teaching that started earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא point begun earlier on the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A food takes on the חטאת's status only through absorption, not mere contact.

steps.title: Only the touching part becomes disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the whole piece becomes פסול when only part of it touched. It answers from the word 'יגע' that only the part that touched is פסול, so you cut that part away.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that if the חטאת touched part of a piece, the whole piece is פסול. The פסוק says 'shall touch,' meaning only what touches is פסול. So what do you do? You cut off the spot that absorbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: that one small touch ruins the whole piece. It then uses the פסוק to reject that idea and gives a practical fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יגע' focuses the law on the exact spot of contact. Because of that, the rest of the piece stays fine, and you only need to slice off the part that absorbed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think' — opens a possible wrong conclusion
'The פסוק teaches' — introduces the proof from the verse
'How so?' — asks how the rule works in practice

phrases.english: One might think: if it touched part of a piece,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the חטאת; the piece is the other food.

phrases.english: the whole of it should be disqualified?
The verse teaches: "shall touch" —
the part that touches is disqualified.
How so?
He cuts off the place that absorbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל נָגַע בְּמִקְצָת חֲתִיכָה יְהֵא כּוּלּוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second detail from the same פסוק: how much of the piece is affected
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the part that absorbed is פסול; it is cut away and the rest is fine.

steps.title: Only the meat passes on the status
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'בבשרה' the ברייתא learns that touching the sinews, bones, horns or hooves of the חטאת does not pass on its status.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Its flesh' — and not the sinews, not the bones, not the horns, and not the hooves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now reads the word 'its flesh' narrowly. Only contact with the actual meat matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names 'flesh,' so other parts of the animal are left out. Food that touches those parts does not take on the חטאת's status.

phrases.english: "Its flesh" — and not the sinews,
and not the bones, and not the horns,
and not the hooves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another limit learned from the same פסוק, this time on which part of the חטאת counts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only contact with the meat of the חטאת counts; sinews, bones, horns and hooves do not.

steps.title: The touching food becomes like the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: From 'יקדש' the ברייתא learns that the touching food takes on the חטאת's status. If the חטאת is פסולה, the food becomes פסול. If it is כשרה, the food is eaten under the חטאת's stricter rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shall be holy' — to be like it. How so? If it is disqualified, the food becomes disqualified. If it is valid, the food is eaten by the stricter rules of the חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the last word of the פסוק. Whatever absorbs from the חטאת gets the same status as the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works in both directions. A פסולה חטאת makes the food פסול. A כשרה חטאת makes the food follow the stricter eating rules of the חטאת, for example that only male כהנים may eat it, and only for one day and one night. This first case, the פסולה חטאת, is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall be holy' — the last word of the פסוק
To be like it, to take on its status
By the stricter rules of it

phrases.english: "Shall be holy" — to be like it.
How so?
If it is disqualified, it becomes disqualified,
phrases.notes: The first 'it' is the חטאת; the second 'it' is the food that touched it.

phrases.english: and if it is valid,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets, but the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: it is eaten according to the stricter of its rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the word 'בבשרה' to the word 'יקדש' in the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food that absorbs from a חטאת takes its status: פסול if the חטאת is פסולה, and eaten under the stricter rules if it is כשרה.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא on 'כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש' teaches four things. There must be absorption. Only the touching spot is affected, and it is cut off. Only the meat counts. The food becomes like the חטאת, whether פסול or כשר.

steps.title: Why doesn't the מצוה of eating override the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why kosher sacrificial meat that absorbed from a פסולה חטאת should be forbidden. Shouldn't the עשה of eating the meat push aside the לא תעשה against eating the absorbed פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let the positive commandment come and push aside the prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that the food 'becomes disqualified' when the חטאת is פסולה. It uses the general rule that an עשה can override a לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sacrificial meat carries a מצוה to eat it, which is an עשה. Eating the absorbed פסול material is a לא תעשה. Normally עשה דוחה לא תעשה, so the גמרא asks why that rule doesn't let us eat the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment (here, eating sacrificial meat)
And let it push aside / override

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is only about the case of a פסולה חטאת making kosher meat forbidden. It is not about the כשרה case.

phrases.english: Why?

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵיתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְלִידְחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה!
phrases.english: Let the positive commandment come and override the prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? וְנֵיתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְלִידְחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling 'אם פסולה היא תפסל' from the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that meat touching a פסולה חטאת becomes forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה should let the מצוה of eating the sacrificial meat override the prohibition on the absorbed פסול.

steps.title: רבא: no overriding for Temple prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה that relates to the מקדש. Step 7 brings his proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A positive commandment does not override a prohibition that relates to the Temple,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives an answer to the challenge by limiting the rule of עשה דוחה לא תעשה. The גמרא will keep going with his statement right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule has an exception: prohibitions that belong to the מקדש are not pushed aside by an עשה. The prohibition on eating the absorbed פסול is one of these, so it stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment does not override

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the well-known rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה does not apply everywhere. Prohibitions connected to the מקדש are treated as an exception.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A positive commandment does not override
a prohibition that relates to the Temple,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the general rule: עשה דוחה לא תעשה does not apply to prohibitions of the מקדש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any עשה, including eating sacrificial meat, overrides any לא תעשה
steps.terutzMaskana: Prohibitions relating to the מקדש are not overridden by an עשה, so the meat stays forbidden

steps.title: Proof from the bones of the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא about breaking bones of the קרבן פסח. It shows that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה connected to the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'Do not break a bone of it.' רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says the ban covers a bone that has marrow and a bone that has none. Why should that be? The עשה of eating the meat should push aside the לא תעשה. So it must be that an עשה does not push aside a לא תעשה connected to the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is proving the rule he just stated. He uses the case of breaking a קרבן פסח bone to get at the marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marrow is part of the meat, so eating it would fulfill the עשה of eating the קרבן פסח. Even so, רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids breaking a bone that has marrow inside. This shows that the עשה cannot override a לא תעשה that belongs to the מקדש, which is exactly רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not break a bone of it (the ban on breaking bones of the קרבן פסח)
Let the positive command come and push aside the prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the general rule that the usual 'עשה overrides לא תעשה' principle does not apply to prohibitions connected to the מקדש.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And a bone you shall not break in it."
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
Both a bone that has marrow in it,
and a bone that has no marrow in it.
Why?
phrases.notes: He means: why forbid breaking a bone that has marrow, when breaking it lets you eat the marrow?

phrases.aramaic: נֵיתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְלִידְחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה!
phrases.english: Let the positive command come and push aside the prohibition!
Rather, a positive command does not push aside
a prohibition that relates to the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by bringing his source.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה connected to the מקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא in a ברייתא about breaking bones of the קרבן פסח

steps.title: רב אשי: an עשה and a לא תעשה stand together
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. The word 'יקדש' is itself an עשה, and one עשה cannot override a לא תעשה joined by another עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'It shall become holy' is a positive command. A positive command does not push aside a prohibition together with a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from Step 5 in another way. He does not need רבא's special rule about the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food that absorbed from the פסולה חטאת is forbidden by a לא תעשה. It also falls under the עשה of 'יקדש', which tells us to treat the food like the חטאת. With an עשה and a לא תעשה both on the forbidding side, the single עשה of eating the meat is not strong enough to override them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall become holy' (ויקרא 6:20), which רב אשי reads as a positive command
A prohibition and a positive command together

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not disagreeing with the final ruling, because both agree the food stays forbidden. He is only giving a different reason why the עשה of eating cannot override the prohibition.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"Shall become holy" is a positive command,
and a positive command does not push aside
a prohibition together with a positive command.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question that רבא answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the conflict as one עשה against a combined לא תעשה and עשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like a simple case of one עשה against one לא תעשה, where the עשה should win.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יקדש' adds an עשה on the forbidding side, so the עשה of eating cannot override both.

steps.title: Do other offerings also pass on status by absorption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that other קדשים, not only a חטאת, pass on their status to food that absorbs from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found that a חטאת passes on its holiness through what is absorbed. From where do we know this for the rest of the קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The פסוק of 'יקדש' speaks only about a חטאת, so what about other offerings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2 to 4 learned the rules of absorption from the חטאת section in ויקרא 6. The גמרא now wants a source that applies these rules to every type of קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
From where do we know it for the other offerings?

phrases.english: We have found that a sin offering
passes on its holiness through what is absorbed,
the rest of the sacred offerings, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן חַטָּאת דְּמִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת בְּבִלּוּעַ, שְׁאָר קָדָשִׁים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עשה question and returns to the absorption rule, asking how far it reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that all קדשים pass on their status through absorption

steps.title: The verse that lists all the offerings together
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, in the name of רבי אליעזר, quotes the פסוק that lists all the offerings in one sentence, which links their laws together.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said in the name of רבי אליעזר: 'This is the law of the עולה, the מנחה, the חטאת, the אשם, the מלואים, and the שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question with a פסוק that groups all the offerings together. The גמרא will now explain what this grouping teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the offerings are listed side by side, a law said about one of them can be applied to the others. This lets the absorption law of the חטאת spread to all קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The inauguration offerings brought when the משכן was dedicated

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
"This is the law of the burnt offering and of the meal offering
and of the sin offering and of the guilt offering
and of the inauguration offerings and of the sacrifice of peace offerings."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ויקרא 7:37 links all the offerings, so the חטאת's absorption law applies to all of them.

steps.title: From the עולה: every offering needs a utensil
steps.stepSummary: The first lesson from the list: just as an עולה needs a utensil, so does every offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of the עולה' means all offerings are like an עולה. Just as an עולה needs a utensil, so too all offerings need a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins going through the list word by word, starting with what the word 'עולה' teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offering in the list adds one law that is shared by all the others. From the עולה, the shared law is that a utensil is needed. The גמרא has not yet said which utensil.

phrases.english: "Of the burnt offering": like a burnt offering;
just as a burnt offering requires a utensil,
so too all require a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining what each word of the פסוק teaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the עולה we learn that all offerings require a utensil.

steps.title: Which utensil? Not the blood bowl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which utensil is meant. It rejects the blood bowl, because that is already written about the שלמי ציבור at הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which utensil? If you say a bowl for blood, it is already written about the communal peace offerings: 'And משה took half of the blood and put it in basins.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which utensil the עולה teaches about, and pushes back against the first guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first guess is the מזרק, the bowl that collects the blood. But the פסוק about the offerings at הר סיני already shows the שלמי ציבור used basins for blood. So we would not need the עולה to teach this, and the guess falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A bowl used to collect the blood
Peace offerings brought for the whole community

phrases.english: What utensil?
If you say a bowl,
with communal peace offerings it is also written about them:
"And Moshe took half of the blood
and put it in basins"!
phrases.notes: שמות 24:6. So the blood bowl is already written about the שלמים, and we don't need the עולה to teach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what Step 11's 'utensil' means and rejects the first possibility.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the utensil learned from the עולה is the blood bowl
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bowl for blood is already written about the שלמי ציבור, so learning it from the עולה would teach nothing new.

steps.title: The utensil is the slaughtering knife
steps.stepSummary: Since the blood bowl is already known, the 'utensil' learned from עולה must be the knife used for שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from the last step. The 'utensil' every offering needs is a knife for slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood bowl could not be the lesson, because we already know it from the שלמי ציבור at הר סיני. So the lesson must be something new: every offering has to be slaughtered with a real knife, not a sharp stone or reed.

phrases.english: Rather, it is of a knife.
phrases.notes: He means the 'utensil' that every offering needs, just like an עולה, is the knife for שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 12 by choosing the knife instead of the bowl.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of which utensil is meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The utensil might be the bowl for the blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The utensil is the slaughtering knife.

steps.title: How do we know an עולה itself needs a knife?
steps.stepSummary: The whole lesson is built on the עולה, so the גמרא asks for the source that an עולה needs a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the עולה itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the starting point: how do we know that an עולה needs a knife? It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the other offerings learn from the עולה. That only works if the עולה rule has its own source, so the גמרא checks that base first.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And the burnt offering itself, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the base case used in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that an עולה must be slaughtered with a knife.

steps.title: Proof from אברהם at the עקידה
steps.stepSummary: אברהם took a knife, and what he brought was an עולה, so an עולה needs a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And אברהם stretched out his hand and took the knife.' And there it was an עולה, as it is written: 'And he brought it up as an עולה instead of his son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the story of the עקידה. אברהם used a knife, and the פסוק calls his offering an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים are put together. The first shows that a knife was used. The second shows that the offering was an עולה. Together they teach that an עולה is slaughtered with a knife.

keyTerms.meaning: Knife, the word used in the עקידה story

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Abraham stretched out his hand
and took the knife"
and there it was a burnt offering,
as it is written: "And he offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son."
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:13. This is the ram אברהם brought in place of יצחק.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עקידה: אברהם used a knife for what the פסוק calls an עולה.
steps.whatToRemember: Lesson one from the list: every offering needs a knife, just like an עולה. The עולה learns it from אברהם's knife at the עקידה.

steps.title: Second lesson: all offerings are eaten only by male כהנים
steps.stepSummary: From the word מנחה in the list: just as a מנחה is eaten only by male כהנים, so are all the offerings in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'מנחה': just as a מנחה is eaten only by male כהנים, so too all of them are eaten only by male כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the list, מנחה, and draws a second lesson from it. Only male כהנים may eat these offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because all the offerings sit in one פסוק, a rule of the מנחה is passed on to the others. Here the rule is who may eat it: male כהנים only.

phrases.english: "Meal offering":
phrases.notes: This is the next word in the list of offerings in ויקרא 7:37.

phrases.english: just as a meal offering is not eaten
except by males of the priesthood,
so too all of them are not eaten
except by males of the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחָה – מָה מִנְחָה אֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לְזִכְרֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the second lesson from the פסוק quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All offerings in the list are eaten only by male כהנים, like a מנחה.

steps.title: חטאת and אשם already have this rule written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offering needs this lesson. It cannot be חטאת or אשם, because the Torah says so about them openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is it for? If חטאת and אשם, it is openly written about them: 'Every male among the כהנים shall eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lesson by asking which offering it is needed for. חטאת and אשם are ruled out, because the Torah already says this about them directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lesson from the list should teach something we did not already know. Since the פסוקים about חטאת and אשם openly limit eating to male כהנים, the lesson cannot be for them.

phrases.english: Which is it?
phrases.notes: He means: which offering do we actually need this lesson for?

phrases.english: If the sin offering and guilt offering,
it is explicitly written about them:
"Every male among the priests shall eat it"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:22 for חטאת, and ויקרא 7:6 for אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא? אִי חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם – בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the lesson of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson from מנחה that only male כהנים eat the offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lesson is not needed for חטאת and אשם, because their פסוקים already say it.

steps.title: שלמי ציבור already have their own source too
steps.stepSummary: The lesson is not needed for שלמי ציבור either, because a ברייתא learns them from an extra phrase in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if for שלמי ציבור, that comes from the extra words of a פסוק: 'In the holiest place you shall eat it, every male shall eat it.' This teaches about שלמי ציבור that they are eaten only by male כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the next possibility. The lesson cannot be for שלמי ציבור, since they already have a source of their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'every male shall eat it' seem extra, and a ברייתא learns from them that שלמי ציבור are eaten only by male כהנים. So every offering we can think of already has a source, and the lesson from the list seems useless.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal peace offerings, the two lambs brought on שבועות
An extra phrase in a פסוק that adds a law

phrases.english: And if it is for communal peace offerings,
that comes from the extra wording of the verse:
"In the most holy place you shall eat it;
every male shall eat it":
it taught about communal peace offerings
that they are eaten only by males of the priesthood!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי שַׁלְמֵי צִיבּוּר – מֵרִיבּוּיָיא דִּקְרָא אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the challenge: it rules out the last remaining option after step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson from מנחה that only male כהנים eat the offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמי ציבור are already learned from the extra words in במדבר 18:10, so the lesson has no job left.

steps.title: It depends on a disagreement between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the need for this lesson depends on a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer: the question depends on a disagreement between תנאים. It is setting up an explanation that comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is saying that the challenge of steps 17 and 18 rests on one side of a disagreement between תנאים. Which תנאים disagree, and about what, is explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the lesson is useless. It is saying the challenge only works according to one opinion, and the other opinion still needs this lesson.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of steps 17 and 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic disagreement: the challenge holds only according to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every offering already has its own source, so the lesson from מנחה is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The need for the lesson from מנחה depends on a disagreement between תנאים, which the גמרא spells out on the next amud.
